drills.q: Name the two operations that cause a virtual thread to pin its carrier, and which JDK version fixed one of them.
drills.a: synchronized blocks/methods (fixed in JDK 24, JEP 491) and native/JNI calls (still pins in JDK 25).

drills.q: True or false: adding a fourth implementor to a sealed interface silently compiles as long as existing switches have a default branch.
drills.a: True in effect, but that defeats the point -- an exhaustive switch with no default would instead fail to compile, forcing every dispatch site to be updated. A default branch reopens the hole sealing was meant to close.

drills.q: Can a record have a mutable field? Why or why not.
drills.a: No. Every component of a record is implicitly private final by design -- records are value types, not general-purpose classes.

drills.q: A service migrates to virtual threads and throughput plateaus below expectation with carrier threads reported idle elsewhere. What's the first thing to check, and what JDK-version-specific detail matters?
drills.a: Check for synchronized blocks pinning virtual threads to carriers -- if pre-JDK 24, this is the known synchronized-block pinning issue (fixed by JEP 491 in JDK 24); if JDK 24+, check for native/JNI calls instead, which still pin.

drills.q: Explain why ThreadLocal is a worse fit than ScopedValue at virtual-thread scale, specifically.
drills.a: Millions of short-lived virtual threads each touching ThreadLocal.set() means millions of per-thread allocations, plus leak risk if remove() in finally is forgotten (state bleeds into a reused pooled thread). ScopedValue is bound only for a scope's duration and auto-unbinds on exit -- no leak by construction, and avoids the per-thread-instance allocation pattern.

drills.q: Why does moving a CPU-bound image-processing workload from a fixed platform-thread pool to virtual-thread-per-task NOT improve throughput?
drills.a: Virtual threads fix I/O-bound thread scalability by unmounting from the carrier while blocked. A CPU-bound task never blocks -- it occupies its carrier for its full duration exactly like a platform thread would, so more virtual threads just means more contention for the same core count, with added scheduling overhead.

drills.q: Is Structured Concurrency (JEP 505) safe to treat as a stable, finalized API in a Java 25 interview answer?
drills.a: No -- it is still in preview (sixth preview round in JDK 25). Claiming it's finalized is a specific, checkable mistake; the correct answer names the preview status.

drills.q: Design question: an I/O-heavy service needs to pick between virtual threads with blocking clients and full Reactor/Netty. What's the default, and when do you deviate?
drills.a: Default to virtual threads with blocking-style clients for most I/O-bound services -- plain sequential code, normal stack traces, easy onboarding. Deviate to full reactive only when measured requirements sit at the genuine top throughput tier, where cited 2025-2026 benchmarks still show reactive Netty ahead by roughly 25-30% over virtual-thread stacks on some workloads.

drills.q: A team ships a fixed platform-thread pool of 200 threads for downstream calls taking 100ms each. What's the theoretical max throughput, and why is that a hard ceiling regardless of downstream speed?
drills.a: 200 concurrent / 0.1s = 2,000 req/s. It's a hard ceiling because each in-flight call permanently occupies one pooled thread until it returns; no thread means no new call can start, independent of how fast the downstream could actually respond if given more concurrency.

drills.q: Explain the bug class Structured Concurrency fixes that manual ExecutorService + Future.get() does not prevent.
drills.a: With manual Futures, there's no enforced relationship between a parent task and the children it spawned -- if the parent times out or stops caring, nothing automatically cancels still-running children, so they keep consuming resources for a result that will never be used. StructuredTaskScope ties subtask lifetime to the enclosing scope, so exiting it (normally, by exception, or by joiner fail-fast) cancels any subtasks still running.

drills.q: A record-based DTO deserializes via Jackson but every field silently comes back as a default value. What's the likely cause?
drills.a: The Jackson version lacks native record support for the canonical constructor (needs jackson-module-parameter-names or an explicit @JsonCreator on older versions, better handled natively in 2.15+). Confirm the Jackson version, or annotate the canonical constructor explicitly.
